subject: NavSync quant roll v2.3.1 — throughput drop & error surge
messages:
From: Tom Blake <tom.blake@navsync.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: NavSync SRE <sre@navsync.com>
Date: 2028-12-01T09:12:00Z
Subject: NavSync quant roll v2.3.1 — immediate throughput drop

Rafael,

We just observed a severe regression minutes after your team rolled v2.3.1 with the q8-compact quant profile to our production routing. Summary: p99 latency jumped ~5x, 500s spiked to ~12% of requests for our checkout API, and overall throughput for the service is down ~60%. This is impacting live checkouts across multiple regions.

We've attached the ops log (navsync-ops-12-01.log) and a short set of traces. The majority of 500s are gRPC timeouts originating from the inference tier. We rolled no other changes on our side. Please advise immediate rollback options and if you can prioritize an emergency canary patch.

Impact: checkout conversions down ~28% in the last 30m (we're seeing real revenue impact).

Tom Blake
Head of SRE, NavSync
Tom.Blake@navsync.com

--- attached: navsync-ops-12-01.log (text) ---

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Tom Blake <tom.blake@navsync.com>
Cc: NavSync SRE <sre@navsync.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-12-01T09:35:00Z
Subject: Re: NavSync quant roll v2.3.1 — immediate throughput drop

Tom — thanks for the quick heads-up and the logs. Sorry you're hitting this. We're treating as priority P0. Looping in CS, ops and applied-ML to stabilize. Initial plan: 

- Triage (10–30m): collect traces, confirm error signatures and whether it's strictly q8-compact related.
- Short-term mitigation (30–90m): initiate canary rollback to the previous model build (v2.2.9) for your traffic or route a percentage to v2.2.9 while we diagnose.
- Longer-term (24–72h): full postmortem, targeted quant-profile re-tuning, and test harness to prevent similar regressions.

Can you confirm the affected routes (checkout-v1, checkout-v2), any pinned model versions on your side, and whether you want an immediate full rollback or a staged canary? We'll prepare rollback playbook ready to execute pending your go.

Rafael Mendes
Account Executive — Strategic
Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com

To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Tom Blake <tom.blake@navsync.com>
Cc: NavSync SRE <sre@navsync.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-12-01T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: NavSync quant roll v2.3.1 — immediate throughput drop

Tom / Rafael — I'm on this. Quick customer-facing plan: 

1) Immediate: we recommend an emergency canary rollback to v2.2.9 for 100% of checkout traffic for the next 30–60 minutes to stop the customer-facing impact. We will estimate credits after containment.
2) Ops: Priyom will run a config to route traffic + collect traces; we'll freeze further quant changes to that model family for 72h.
3) Post-containment: joint RCA with NavSync SRE + Applied ML to identify quant-decoding mismatch and create additional unit tests.

Please see the attached mutual action plan (navsync-map.xlsx) — I've sketched an immediate rollback window and owners. Tom — can you confirm a 30–60m rollback window that minimizes revenue loss?

Marissa Cole
Customer Success
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Tom Blake <tom.blake@navsync.com>
Cc: NavSync SRE <sre@navsync.com>
Date: 2028-12-01T10:40:00Z
Subject: Re: NavSync quant roll v2.3.1 — immediate throughput drop

Quick ops notes and observations from the cluster: 

- Observed behavior: model workers running v2.3.1 + q8-compact are showing significantly higher per-token CPU and increased KV-cache churn for the checkout request shape. This results in request queue growth and gRPC deadline_exceeded errors.
- Immediate mitigation commands (ready to run once we have Tom's GO):
  * redwoodctl rollout set --account navsync --model mymodel:v2.2.9 --route checkout-v1 --percentage 100 
  * redwoodctl monitor logs --account navsync --filter "deadline_exceeded" --since 15m
- Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/rollback (internal)
- Evidence: attaching a short dump of error signatures (we've also pushed traces to the shared Drive).

If you want a more surgical approach we can route 80% -> v2.2.9, 20% -> v2.3.1 for 15 minutes to validate recovery, but given revenue impact I'd recommend full immediate rollback.

Priyom Das
SRE — Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.com

From: Tom Blake <tom.blake@navsync.com>

Cc: NavSync SRE <sre@navsync.com>, Lauren Meyers <lauren.meyers@lauren.meyers@navsync.com>
Date: 2028-12-01T11:06:00Z
Subject: Re: NavSync quant roll v2.3.1 — immediate throughput drop

Thanks — we ran a short internal test routing 50% traffic -> v2.2.9 and saw the checkout success rate return to baseline within ~90s. Can you confirm you'll execute the full rollback? We need the rollback window ASAP — each 15m of degradation is material for us.

One note for the RCA: the failures disproportionately affect requests with longer context (checkout carts with >8 items) — looks correlated with sequence length. We're opening JIRA NAVSYNC-1423 and will share more traces shortly.

Tom Blake
Head of SRE, NavSync

> > Tom — thanks for the quick heads-up and the logs...

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Tom Blake <tom.blake@navsync.com>
Cc: NavSync SRE <sre@navsync.com>
Date: 2028-12-05T16:23:00Z
Subject: Re: NavSync quant roll v2.3.1 — throughput drop & error surge — rollback plan and next steps

Team — quick summary and concrete timeline after our internal deep-dive: 

Executive summary: the v2.3.1 model binary is fine in isolation, but the q8-compact quant profile introduces decoding contention for long-sequence checkout requests which increases per-request compute and KV churn. This manifests as queueing and gRPC deadline_exceeded in your production shape.

Immediate plan (approved):
- 2028-12-05T18:00:00Z: execute emergency canary rollback for NavSync's checkout-v1/v2 routes to v2.2.9 (full traffic). Priyom will run the redwoodctl command and monitor for error regression.
- 18:00–18:30Z: validate p99 latency and error rate return to baseline; if stable, keep v2.2.9 pinned for 72h.
- Post-containment (24–72h): joint RCA, re-run quant sensitivity tests on long-sequence workloads, and introduce a pre-deploy synthetic that mimics NavSync checkout patterns.

We're also preparing a small customer credit to offset measurable revenue loss during the incident window (Rafael will coordinate approvals). Attached is the canary rollback playbook (canary-rollback-plan.md) and the proposed MAP we discussed (navsync-map.xlsx).

I'll lead the postmortem with NavSync SRE and Applied ML; target delivery is 2028-12-08 EOD. Rafael — please advise if you want leadership looped for further credits/exec briefing.

Irene Choi
Director, Applied ML — Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.com
